headline: Airbyte’s broad network egress creates the main risk; python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and largely blocks direct pairwise harm.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. agent_a has broad network egress and Airbyte API access, but agent_b has no stdin/stdout, clipboard, files, MCP, or browser surfaces, so there is no plausible default path for agent_a content to hijack agent_b instructions.
conditions: IF agent_b is later connected to a shared clipboard, file mount, or message queue with agent_a, prompt-injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not add clipboard or file-based handoff between them.
Avoid routing agent_a outputs into agent_b prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches business data and has broad network egress, but agent_b is documentation-only with no filesystem read/write, no API calls, and no network egress. The pair does not show a default path for agent_b to exfiltrate agent_a data; any leakage would require unusual external wiring.
conditions: IF agent_b is given access to the same workspace or receives agent_a outputs as files, leakage risk increases.
IF agent_b is connected to a networked backend, it could relay copied content.
mitigations: Keep business data out of agent_b prompts.
Use separate storage locations for each agent.
Disable any future file handoff unless reviewed.
requires-engineering: add DLP checks on any shared output channel.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can call the Airbyte API and has broad egress, while agent_b cannot write files, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, or use MCP. With no overlapping write surface or shared mutable resource documented, there is no plausible capability conflict in the default pair.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or mutable API, conflict risk becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep agent_b read-only.
Avoid sharing mutable resources between the agents.
Do not grant agent_b filesystem or git write permissions.
requires-engineering: add locking if a shared mutable backend is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b is a cheatsheet/reference agent, not an action-taking system, and it has no stdin/stdout or API surface. Even if agent_a produces incorrect business-data outputs, agent_b is not documented to consume them authoritatively or execute downstream actions, so cascading error is limited.
conditions: IF agent_b is repurposed to draft or execute actions from agent_a outputs, cascading error risk rises.
IF agent_a outputs are manually copied into agent_b as authoritative facts, errors can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review of any agent_a-derived content.
Do not treat agent_a outputs as source of truth.
Keep agent_b in reference-only mode.
requires-engineering: add verification steps before any downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented. agent_a touches business data and agent_b touches no data classes, so there is no evidenced compliance pathway between them in the default configuration.
conditions: IF regulated data is later routed through agent_b, compliance review is required.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of agent_b.
Document any future data-sharing path.
Review retention settings before connecting the agents.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement if regulated data flows are introduced.
